Apple's new iPhone Handoff feature lets users share the same phone number across two iPhones — and it will cost T-Mobile customers an extra $5 per month. Here's what you need to know.

Deutsche Telekom also requires a subscription for the service

Earlier this year, during a WWDC keynote, Apple flashed a slide listing the dozens of features and improvements coming in iOS 27, including 'switching the same phone number between two iPhones.'

At yesterday's 'Surprise and Shine' event, Apple's iPhone product marketing VP Kaiann Drance shared more details about the feature:

But what wasn't mentioned at the event is that, at least for T-Mobile customers, the feature will cost an extra $5 per month, as Stetson Doggett pointed out on X:

Popular comment from Brent Plummer

Seems cheaper than adding a second line, but no one's going to be happy about it. At least it's not the $10+ some carriers charge for Apple Watch.

If you've got deep pockets and want to run both a Duo and a Pro at the same time, this is kind of fun. I bet this was largely developed by Apple employees because they swap phones so often.

Apple's iPhone Handoff support page states 'carrier fees may apply when adding iPhone Handoff' and recommends customers check with their carrier for more details.

9to5Mac dug into Deutsche Telekom's published information about the feature and found that the carrier does not charge extra for iPhone Handoff.

However, the feature is part of the carrier's MultiSIM service. Adding MultiSIM to an existing plan costs €6.95 per month, though some select plans already include a SIM at no extra charge.
